To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the impact of 3D-printing on business model innovation is limited in rapid prototyping and in rapid tooling, but is significant in direct manufacturing and in home fabrication.
3D Printing Technologies are a game changer for business model innovation because they allow to: (1) create value at a much lower cost and (2) adapt the business model much faster.

1. 3D printing can be a source of innovation for all the components of the business model, 2. the impact of 3D on the business model is different depending on the phase of adoption of 3D, 3. business model innovation can be carried out in a ‘rapid prototyping way’, and 4. the ‘rapid prototyper’ paradigm is a key enabler of the business model innovation in the home fabrication phase.

3D Printing is changing business model innovations by enabling adaptive business model innovation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

while 3D printing has the potential to change business models in fundamental ways, it will not do so automatically, and the way business model evolution will occur will depend on the extent of adoption of these technologies in the production process.
the business model innovation process needs to be more agile to adapt to the new environment and that business model innovation needs to be more iterative to be successful.

the impact of 3D Printing on business model innovation is highly dependent on the stage of the 3D Printing revolution in which a firm operates, and the business model innovation process needs to be rethought to accommodate for the specificities of each phase of the revolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3D technologies will be disruptive, but not in the way we have been led to believe by the hype.
business model innovation is a key factor in the success of 3D printed products and services.
3D technologies are likely to have a major impact on business model innovation, which should not be underestimated by business managers.
